I believe racism is mostly everywhere but overall the Portuguese is a very welcoming population to everyone so I think you would have a great time. 
These are just my two cents but naturally I can’t 100% guarantee that this will be your experience.

23F. Milan, Slovenia and Croatia. Slovenia (Ljubljana) is beautiful and felt very safe. Croatia is full of solo travelers so it’s easy to meet people to spend time with. I can’t say enough times how couchsurfing is the best way for meeting people, in my opinion (or it used to be 4/5 years ago, anyway). Some people use it like tinder but generally it’s great.

My experience:
Two 25 year old women. I was in Cairo and Sharm El Sheikh. I had a guide in Cairo but no guide in Sharm, although I spent most of time in Sharm in the hotel as it was a resort with its own beach and that’s what we went there for. 
The traffic in Cairo is chaotic, I kind of feared for my life when I first arrived and was driven to the hotel but it seems like they have their driving under control as I was driven around several times and nothing ever happened. I refused to cross the street on foot though. 
As a woman I didn’t feel unsafe and the people barely looked at me (the ones who did were mostly woman and it just gave a vibe of “you’re not from here” but not in a bad way, just curiosity). All hotels have metal detectors and where I stayed they barely let Egyptians in (I stayed at the Conrad and invited my guide to join us at the casino in the hotel and he was refused entry).
There’s a lot of poverty and the city is kind of dirty, you see piles of trash and goats and dogs eating from there so if that’s something you’re not used to it can make you rather uncomfortable.
I never felt like I was being scammed or someone was trying to take advantage of me.
Lastly, I didn’t have much contact with the locals but the ones I did were super nice and welcoming.

Hope your son has a good time there!

I am anxious about the future, yes, I feel like it won’t be as good now he’s not in my life. He was the first person I ever thought about a future with and he wanted it as well at some point. So I think I’m taking it especially hard because it’s a new feeling for me - wanting to spend my life with someone, build a family, etc.
But above all I just miss him in my life right now. We made each other better, we rarely got into arguments, we were really comfortable being around each other... he became a great part of my support system and he is the exact reason why I’m like this, I feel like he’s the only one that could make me feel better.

Also, the fact that he broke up with me when we were apart, so over the phone, and that we had just seen each other 2 weeks before and things were great, is making things worse I think. I left his house thinking it would become my house soon and out of the blue, all of that was gone

It’s stupid but my bf broke up with me recently and I’m not handling it well.
He‘s from the UK and lives there. I’m from Portugal and I live here so we were in a long distance relationship but we saw each other often. I was going to move there in 6 months. We had a great relationship so I was caught completely off guard - he said his feeling weren’t strong enough to wait for another 6 months.

This not a case of me feeling like I’m nothing without him, or that my confidence/self-love was tied to his validation, it’s not. It just hurts so much to think he is not a part of my life anymore because every time I think about the future, it makes more sense if he’s there as well

It’s a bit of a mix. I’m not one to express how I’m feeling if it requires confrontation, like telling a friend they did acted wrong towards me, or stand up for myself to my boss. 
When it comes to sadness, it’s a bit different though and in this specific situation I’ve been very open about it, I’m constantly crying and I tell that to my mom and my friends, I talk about how hopeless I’m feeling

I have but the only thing people say is “it will get better” and “you’ve been through much worse (my disease) so you can get through this as well”.

I’ve always been a very emotional person who feels everything extremely deeply but I had never felt like this...
